                        LOS ANGELES CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
                              OFFICIAL MEETING MINUTES
                       THURSDAY, JULY 9, 2026 REGULAR MEETING
                  LOS ANGELES CITY HALL, COUNCIL CHAMBER, ROOM 340
                200 NORTH SPRING STREET, LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90012

MINUTES OF THE LOS ANGELES CITY PLANNING COMMISSION HEREIN ARE REPORTED IN
ACTION FORMAT. THE ENTIRE DISCUSSION RELATED TO EACH ITEM IS ACCESSIBLE IN AUDIO
FORMAT ONLINE AT planning.lacity.org. TO LISTEN TO THE AUDIO FILE: SELECT “ABOUT”,
“COMMISSIONS, BOARDS & HEARINGS”, FILTER BY “CITY PLANNING COMMISSION”, LOCATE
THE COMMISSION MEETING DATE AND SELECT THE “AUDIO” BUTTON.

The City Planning Commission regular meeting of July 9, 2026 was conducted in person in Los Angeles
City Hall, Council Chamber, Room 340 and via Zoom webinar in a hybrid meeting format.

Commission Vice President Caroline Choe called the meeting to order at 8:32 a.m. with Commissioners
Priscilla Chavez, Martina Diaz, Sarah Johnson, Phyllis Klein, Brian Rosenstein, Jacob Saitman, and
Elizabeth Zamora in attendance.

Commission President Monique Lawshe was not in attendance.

Also in attendance were Lisa M. Webber and Haydee Urita-Lopez, Deputy Directors, and Kimberly
Huangfu and Ernesto Velazquez, Deputy City Attorneys. Commission Office Staff participation included
Cecilia Lamas, Commission Executive Assistant II, Diego Vazquez and Marcos G. Godoy, Administrative
Clerks.

                              _______________________________
                                         ITEM NO. 5a

CPC-2023-3247-DB-COA-HCA                                                   Council District: 1 – Hernandez
CEQA: ENV-2023-3248-CE                                                         Last Day to Act: 07-09-26
Plan Area: Northeast Los Angeles

PUBLIC HEARING – Completed April 24, 2026

PROJECT SITE:              217 North Avenue 55

IN ATTENDANCE:
Pablo Estrada, City Planning Associate, Nicole Sanchez and Christina Park, City Planners and Vanessa
Soto, Senior City Planner, representing the Planning Department; and Gustavo Cesareo, representing the
Applicant.

MOTION:
Commissioner Diaz moved to put forth the actions below in conjunction with the following Project, with
Amendments, as stated on the record:

Construction, use, and maintenance of a new three-story, seven-unit apartment building with one unit set
aside for a low-income household, and one unit set aside for a very low-income household towards the
rear of an existing historic duplex. The Project site is a 9,825.5 square foot lot that is zoned RD2-1-HPOZ
and contains an existing historic duplex built in 1907 which is a Contributing Feature to the Highland Park
– Garvanza Historic Preservation Overlay Zone (HPOZ). No changes to the existing historic duplex are
proposed; all new construction will be located at the rear of the lot. The unit mix ranges from one studio,
two units consisting of one bedroom, two units consisting of two bedrooms, and two units consisting of
three bedrooms and the floor area of each dwelling unit will range from 437 to 1,187 square feet. The
Project proposes seven long-term bicycle parking stalls, and two short term bicycle parking stalls. The
Project proposes to grade approximately 570 cubic yards of cut and approximately 100 cubic yards of fill.

1. Determine, based on the whole of the administrative record, that the Project is exempt from the
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Section
   15332 (Class 32 - Infill Development), and there is no substantial evidence demonstrating that an
   exception to a categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section 15300.2 applies;
2. Approve, pursuant to Chapter 1 Section 12.22 A.25 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC), a
   Density Bonus for a Housing Development Project consisting of a new three-story, seven-unit
   apartment building with one unit set aside for a low-income household, and one unit set aside for a
   very low-income household towards the rear of an existing historic duplex, with the following On- Off-
   Menu Incentives:
   a. An Off-Menu Incentive to allow a front access passageway reduction to eight feet in lieu of the 10-
       foot requirement per LAMC Chapter 1 Section 12.21 C.2(b);
   b. An On-Menu Incentive for a reduction in the rear yard setback to 12 feet in lieu of the 15-foot
       requirement per LAMC Chapter 1 Section 12.22 C.10; and
   c. An On-Menu Incentive to permit a 20 percent decrease in the required east side yard setback to
       allow a five-foot side yard setback in lieu of the six feet required by the RD2-1 Zone pursuant to

City Planning Commission                    Meeting Minutes                                    July 9, 2026
       LAMC Chapter 1 Section 12.09.1;
3. Approve, pursuant to LAMC Chapter 1 Section 12.20.3 K, a Certificate of Appropriateness for the
   construction of a new three-story, seven-unit residential building;
4. Adopt Conditions of Approval; and
5. Adopt the Findings, as Amended by the Commission, including Staff’s Technical Modification dated
   July 6, 2026.

Commissioner Klein seconded the motion and the vote proceeded as follows:

Moved:         Diaz
Second:        Klein
Ayes:          Choe, Chavez, Johnson, Rosenstein, Saitman, Zamora
Absent:        Lawshe

Vote:          8–0

MOTION PASSED

                                  _______________________________
                                             ITEM NO. 6

CPC-2025-5194-HD-CU2-PR-ZC                                                          Council District: 10 – Hutt
CEQA: ENV-2025-5195-MND                                                             Last Day to Act: 07-26-26
Plan Area: Wilshire

PUBLIC HEARING – Completed May 12, 2026

PROJECT SITE:                  4802 – 4828 West San Vicente Boulevard

IN ATTENDANCE:
David Woon, Planning Assistant, Esther Ahn, City Planner, and Milena Zasadzien, Principal City Planner,
representing the Planning Department; Dana Sayles, representing the Applicant; and Hakeem Parke-
Davis, representing Council District 10 on behalf of Councilmember Heather Hutt.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rosenstein moved to put forth the actions below in conjunction with the following Project,
with Modifications, as stated on the record:

Demolition and removal of the existing one-story warehouse building and two surface parking lots for the
construction, use, and maintenance of a seven-story self-storage facility for household goods
encompassing a floor area of 161,645 square feet. The self-storage facility would feature storage units
across each floor level, a 954-square-foot office area, a 608-square-foot lobby, a 376-square-foot
community room/multi-purpose room, five vehicular parking spaces, 36 bicycle parking spaces, and two
loading spaces and would operate between 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., daily.

1.   Find, pursuant to Sections 21082.1(c)(3) and 21081.6 of the California Public Resources Code and
     CEQA Guidelines Section 15074(b), after consideration of the whole of the administrative record,
     including the Mitigated Negative Declaration, No. ENV-2025-5195-MND (“Negative Declaration”), and
     all comments received, with the imposition of mitigation measures, there is no substantial evidence
     that the Project will have a significant effect on the environment; Find the Mitigated Negative
     Declaration reflects the independent judgment and analysis of the City; Find the mitigation measures
     have been made enforceable conditions on the Project; and adopt the Mitigated Negative Declaration
     and the Mitigation Monitoring Program prepared for the Mitigated Negative Declaration;
2.   Approve and recommend that City Council adopt the ordinance, pursuant to Chapter 1A Section
     13B.1.4 of the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC), a Change and Height District Change Ordinance,
     from C2-1-O to (T)(Q)C2-2D-O, in order to permit additional floor area up to a maximum Floor Area
     Ratio of 6:1 in lieu of 1.5:1, including a waiver of the requirement to dedicate and improve an additional
     2.5 feet of the existing public alley;
